we have demonstrated K-band low noise amplifiers with good performance in 0. 18 /spl mu /m standard CMOS process.
the parasitic effects have been successfully modeled in our CMOS LNA designs.
the interconnect line parasitics and the pad parasitics have been taken into account in the LNA design and the LNA performance agrees with the simulated one.

the design and characterization of CMOS K-band LNAA.
the design of low noise amplifiers for the K-band.
the design and characterization of the CMOS LNAs for the K-band applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed LNAs are suitable for the 24/26 GHz applications, and can be further scaled to the higher frequency band.

the parasitics of the interconnect transmission line, and the RF pads, can not be neglected in the design of high frequency CMOS LNAs, and the design of high performance CMOS LNAs requires a careful and accurate analysis of the parasitic effects.
the CMOS K-band LNA design is feasible and can be applied to the design of CMOS K-band transceivers for wireless communications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parasitic effect of interconnect line and the RF pad is significant for the LNA design.
we have successfully demonstrated K- band LNAs in 0.1 8/spl mu/m standard CMOs process, and validated their performance.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of K-band LNAs in CMOS process.

the parasitic effects can be accurately modeled and taken into account in the design of RF circuits.
the parasitics of interconnect transmission lines and RF pads should be taken into account for CMOS LNA designs at millimeter-wave frequencies.
